title: A lower median is not a general usability finding
audience: Readers practicing critical interpretation of a small research notebook
question: What can these fictional instruction-card walkthroughs support?
summary: Icons has a lower median, 9 versus 12 seconds, but a wider observed range; these scripted walkthroughs do not establish a population effect.
context: Explicitly fictional research-reading exercise. No real participants, study or published findings are represented.

sources.title: Fictional instruction-card walkthrough notebook
sources.note: Raw times, medians, ranges and the facilitator's qualification are supplied together.

claims.text: Text has median 12 seconds and range 10–14; Icons has median 9 seconds and range 8–16.
claims.scope: Three scripted walkthroughs per card by the same fictional facilitator.
claims.uncertainty: Bounds are the minimum and maximum of three fictional walkthrough times per card, not confidence intervals or population error estimates.

claims.text: The slow Icons walkthrough included a pause at an unfamiliar symbol.
claims.uncertainty: The note does not isolate the symbol as the cause of the pause or of total task time.

claims.text: These notes do not establish that Icons is faster for untrained readers.
claims.basis: The same facilitator performed all scripted walkthroughs, order was not counterbalanced, and no untrained reader is represented.
claims.scope: A limitation of this notebook, not a claim that Icons has no effect.

claims.text: Repeat with untrained readers and counterbalanced order before choosing a format.
claims.scope: A proposed follow-up exercise, not completed research.

beats.title: Read the center and the spread
beats.text: Icons has the lower median, but its slowest scripted walkthrough is slower.
beats.narration: This fictional notebook gives three walkthroughs per card. Text has a median of twelve seconds and a range from ten to fourteen. Icons has a median of nine and a range from eight to sixteen. The bounds show observed minimum and maximum times, not confidence intervals.

visual.title: Median time with supplied min–max bounds
visual.description: Three fictional walkthrough times per card. Icons has a lower median and a wider observed range.
visual.uncertainty_label: Bounds are the minimum and maximum of three fictional walkthrough times per card, not confidence intervals or population error estimates.
visual.caption: Source: walkthrough-notes, conditions and uncertainty_meaning. This is not a real research finding.

question.prompt: Do these bounds estimate uncertainty in a population mean?
question.answer: No. They are the supplied minimum and maximum of three fictional times per card.

beats.title: Keep the note separate from the cause
beats.text: A reported pause is an observation about a walkthrough, not an isolated causal effect.
beats.narration: The fictional facilitator reports a pause at an unfamiliar symbol in the slow Icons walkthrough. The note does not isolate a cause. All walkthroughs use the same facilitator, without counterbalanced order or untrained readers. A lower median here is not a general usability finding.

beats.title: Test the question that remains
beats.text: Propose untrained readers and counterbalanced order.
beats.narration: The proposed next step is to repeat with untrained readers and counterbalanced order before choosing a format. That follow-up has not happened in this fictional notebook.

question.prompt: Does insufficient evidence for a general benefit prove that Icons has no benefit?
question.answer: No. The notebook cannot establish the general effect in either direction.

limitations: All data and attributed notes are fictional and local to this exercise.
Observed min–max ranges are not confidence intervals.
The same facilitator, unbalanced order and missing untrained-reader evidence prevent a general usability conclusion.
